newsitem.title: USA: Certification issue dropped in Mexico-drugs talks.
newsitem.headline: Certification issue dropped in Mexico-drugs talks.

text.p: Key U.S. senators said on Tuesday that a Senate proposal to "decertify" Mexico as an ally in the anti-drug war had been dropped in negotiations with Clinton administration officials.

The move appeared to be a major concession to the administration, which fears a backlash from Mexico. "I think certification (as an issue) is off the table," Sen. Kay Bailey Hutchison, a Texas Republican, told reporters.
California Democrat Dianne Feinstein said in a separate interview that under a proposed compromise, certification of Mexico would continue.
"We would give up on that (decertification) in exchange for having some process that had some accounting for actions in it," she said.
The third senator in negotiations with the administration, Republican Paul Coverdell of Georgia, tentatively scheduled a news conference on the issue later in the day.

Feinstein said that the Senate team "tried to work out something which gave the administration what they wanted and at the same time was real enough to anticipate that some actions (on drugs) are to develop." Feinstein said she did not believe the administration had seen the proposed compromise.
